question: With the publication of the European Grids Package, the Commission confirmed the urgency of reforming Europe’s electricity grids to enable the large-scale integration of renewables, electrification of demand and the achievement of the EU’s energy and climate objectives.

At the same time, key elements of the regulatory framework governing grid connections, namely the EU Connection Network Codes set out in Regulations (EU) 2016/6311, 2016/13882 and 2016/14473, remain outdated. The revision process launched in 2022 has been repeatedly postponed. The Commission has acknowledged these challenges by publishing non-binding guidance on grid connections alongside the European Grids Package.

However, it seems contradictory that the Commission does not prioritise the legal documents for grid connections. In the absence of updated EU-level rules, several Member States are introducing national interim solutions, thereby risking, inter alia, system instability and distortions of the internal market. 1.
How does the Commission assess the consistency between the objectives of the European Grids Package and the continued delay in revising the Connection Network Codes?
What measures will the Commission take to ensure coordination among Member States during this delay?
Does the Commission intend to address urgent technical requirements through interim or phased EU-level updates to the Connection Network Codes, and within what timeframe?

OJ L 112, 27.4.2016, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/631/oj. OJ L 223, 18.8.2016, p. 10, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/1388/oj. OJ L 241, 8.9.2016, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/1447/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.2026) The Commission is continuing work on the Grid Connection Network Codes and is currently focussed on Regulation (EU) 2016/6311, which sets out the rules on requirements for generators. Work on the other Grid Codes will follow.

While these legal instruments are being finalised the Commission has, in the meantime, published a Guidance on grid connections as part of the Grids package2 to support Member States, National Regulatory Authorities and System Operators in addressing grid connection queues within the existing legal framework.

These measures can already be implemented in a safe manner, without creating system instability nor distortions of the internal market. The Commission aims to launch the comitology process in mid-2026 for the Grid Connection Network Codes, starting with Regulation (EU) 2016/631 and the subsequent adoption will provide regulatory certainty for all Member States.
Since the drafting work continues on the Grid Connection Codes, the process is already underway and the Commission does not expect that interim or phased updates will be required.
